KEY MESSAGE 1... 
A weak low pressure system has moved off to the northeast this 
morning with the associated cold front moving across Northern Ohio 
currently. Along this front, showers and thunderstorms have moved 
eastward into Northern Ohio and should continue east-southeast 
through the morning hours. Temperatures and dewpoints across the 
region are in the mid to upper 60s and upper 50s to low 60 
respectively. Current Mesoanalysis has MUCAPE of around 500 J/kg or 
less across the region and 0-6km bulk shear of 45-55 knots where the 
thunderstorms are located. There's ample DCAPE out ahead of the 
front of around 1000, including a plume over the central basin of 
Lake Erie. With the lake being fairly warm still, around 18C, this 
may assist in some thunderstorms over the lake becoming more 
organized in the coming hours. With that being said, severe chances 
are fairly low for this event and if a storm or two does become more 
organized then strong winds will be the main impact. 

The cold front will sag southward over the next several hours before 
settling across the Ohio Valley by midday today. There will be 
potential of moderate to heavy rain with it as it does push south, 
though should be isolated. As the front settles, areas south of the 
US30 corridor may see periodic showers through this evening. 
Overall, not expecting much in terms of rain accumulation for the 
region, with most areas staying around a few tenths to 0.25 inch. 
Exception would be the areas south of the US30 corridor which could 
see up to 0.50 inch. Rain will trend further south throughout the 
day as high pressure begins to build in from the north. Brief period 
of dry weather is expected until Thursday afternoon.  

KEY MESSAGE 2...
An upper level trough will begin to deepen across the Canadian 
Prairies Thursday night into Friday and push eastward into the Great 
Lakes region by Friday afternoon. The associated surface low 
pressure system will develop across the Mid-Mississippi Valley 
Thursday evening morning northeast towards the Great Lakes. The cold 
front that settled across the Ohio Valley today will lift north as a 
warm front Thursday evening into Friday night. Showers and 
thunderstorms will develop along this warm front and move into 
Western Ohio by Thursday evening, moving eastward into Friday. Given 
the timeframe the warm front lifts north, there will be little 
instability across the region and a low level inversion setting up 
with weak lapse rates. Though, low level winds will be fairly strong 
behind the front as the surface low begins to rapidly deepen. Low 
level winds will be 40-50 knots with 0-6km bulk shear around 50-60 
knots. With this, isolated strong to severe wind gusts will be 
possible into early Friday morning. 

The surface low pressure will continue to deepen throughout the day 
Friday as it moves eastward through the Great Lakes. The associated 
cold front will pass west to east across the region during the day 
Friday as well and should be clear of the CWA by Friday evening. 
Severe weather is not expected with the cold front as it moves 
through. There may be some lingering lake effect rain across 
Northeastern Ohio and Northwestern Pennsylvania into early Saturday 
morning with the northerly flow. Some snowflakes could be mixed in 
as well depending on how quickly the precipitation moves out.
Though, given the rapidly deepening low pressure system, the 
pressure gradient will increase behind and winds increase as well. 
Winds will be 15-25 MPH with gusts over 40 MPH from midday Friday 
through the early overnight hours behind the cold front. CAA across 
the region will help in mix down the strong low level winds. Winds 
may reach advisory criteria briefly Friday evening, main areas will 
be along the lakeshore from Lorain County eastward and in 
Northwestern Ohio. Will need to assess the need for an advisory in 
in the coming days. 

With the strong CAA behind the cold front and low pressure system, 
it will bring in the coldest air of the season so far. Overnight 
lows Friday night will be in the mid to upper 30s across much of the 
region. Areas across far Northeastern Ohio and Northwestern 
Pennsylvania may reach freezing temperatures. Widespread Frost 
Advisories and targeted Freeze Warnings will likely be needed for 
that night. Winds may be the a factor keeping frost from occurring 
widespread as they will still be elevated 10-15 MPH for most of the 
overnight period. Saturday night will bring more widespread 
temperatures of near or below freezing. Highest probabilities of 
temperatures at 32 degrees or below will be east of the I-71 
corridor and away from the lakeshore. Winds will have calmed more at 
this point, and with high pressure building in with clearing skies, 
confidence is higher in widespread frost/freeze headlines for this 
period.
